scenes.heading: Gin: Routing, Middleware & Request Binding
scenes.narration: Let's get comfortable with Gin, the fast Go web framework, and its three pillars: routing, middleware, and request binding.

scenes.heading: Three superpowers over net/http
items: A radix-tree router that matches in O(path length)
A middleware chain driven by c.Next() and c.Abort()
Declarative binding with validator struct tags
scenes.narration: Gin keeps net slash http underneath but adds three things. First, a radix-tree router that matches any URL in time proportional to path length, no matter how many routes exist. Second, a first-class middleware chain you drive with c-dot-Next and c-dot-Abort. And third, request binding that decodes and validates input straight into a struct using tags. Together they let you ship clean JSON APIs fast.

scenes.heading: How a request flows
steps: Router matches the path in the radix tree
Middleware runs on the way in
Binding decodes the body into a struct
Middleware code after Next runs on the way out
scenes.narration: Picture a request moving down a conveyor belt. The radix-tree router instantly sorts it onto the right handler chain. Each middleware runs its code, then calls c-dot-Next to invoke the rest of the chain, so code before Next runs on the way in and code after it runs on the way out. Binding unpacks the request body into a typed struct, and your handler works with validated data — or a middleware aborts and short-circuits the whole thing.

scenes.heading: Bind and validate in one step
scenes.narration: The binding tags declare the rules right next to the fields: name is required, email must be a valid address, and age must sit between zero and one thirty. Should-Bind-JSON decodes the body and runs the validator in a single call. On failure it returns the error and writes nothing, so we control the four-hundred response ourselves. Prefer Should-Bind over plain Bind for exactly that reason.

scenes.text: Scope middleware with route groups, centralize errors with c.Error plus a trailing handler, and wrap the engine in your own http.Server.
scenes.narration: Organize routes with groups so auth applies only to protected subtrees, centralize error shaping by recording failures with c-dot-Error and inspecting them in a trailing middleware, and wrap the Gin engine in your own http-dot-Server to get real timeouts and graceful shutdown.
